conclusion.causal: The +247.989 us flash ownership gap is scheduling/critical-path exposure: native serializes 305.581 us while only 57.592 us of llama flash owns exposed time.
conclusion.not_proven: This does not show native flash kernels are optimal, nor predict wall recovery from a kernel rewrite. A native flash rewrite can only be credited by an exact real-token A/B; absent native overlap, its theoretical ceiling is the 305.581 us native serialized population.
conclusion.sufficient: A raw-kernel-speed advantage for llama is not required to explain this ownership gap: llama's own raw flash interval union is 58.135 us larger than native's calibrated raw flash time.

definitions.exposed: disjoint Shapley ownership of llama's non-MMQ interval union; additive by construction
definitions.native: calibrated profile composition within the marker-light DEV=NV device window; stream-ordered
definitions.raw: sum of the class's own interval unions; not an additive token-wall cost when it overlaps MMQ
